title: The Nvidia money trail

lines: erased from the biggest stock in most 401(k)s.
Nvidia's CEO admitted an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
Before the story broke, the US official who approves chip sales to China was sent a classified warning about her.
His agency still cleared about 10 Chinese companies to buy Nvidia's advanced chips.
The Senate now wants both men to testify.
Own an S&P 500 fund? Then you own Nvidia.
This story is about your money.
The scandal isn't the affair. It's who was warned, and what got approved anyway.

caption:
The most important stock in most retirement accounts lost about $1 trillion in market value in a week, per Axios — and its CEO of 33 years is gone.

The part getting less attention: Axios reports the Commerce Secretary was sent a classified warning about the CEO's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy BEFORE his department cleared roughly 10 Chinese companies to buy Nvidia's advanced chips. The Senate now wants both men to testify.

My take: the affair is the headline, but the money story is who was warned, when, and what got approved anyway.

If you hold an S&P 500 fund, Nvidia is in it. Should chip-export approvals get an independent review? 👇
